mira: quick heads-up — ran an equal-conditions comparison between model-A-ggml-35b-q4 and model-B-hf-q4 using both the replay harness and the synthetic loader. saw a 12-18% tail-latency delta that correlates with kernel selection differences, not the model weights. initial numbers below.

jonathan: can you paste the exact harness flags / prompt set you used?

mira: sure — used the standard convo-set-200 prompts (same ordering), deterministic decoding (temp=0, top_k=1), stop sequence: ['\n\n']. replay flags: 
``` 
./bench/replay --manifest=manifests/convo-200.json --seed=42 --deterministic --decode-params='{"temp":0.0,"top_k":1}' --max-tokens=128 --emit=latency,p99,p50
```
synthetic run: 
```
./bench/synth --pattern=prefix+randwords --seq-len=64 --batch-sizes=1,4,8 --decode-params='same' --emit=latency,p99
```

samir: two quick checks that often bite apples-to-apples: tokenizer normalization (NFKC vs NFC) and stop-sequence trimming. even 1 extra token at prompt time changes batching behavior and KV cache hits. did you align the tokenizer configs between models?

mira: good call. i diffed token counts and found model-B tokenizes the em-dash (—) as 2 tokens vs model-A as 1. example: "We tested — on all inputs" -> A: 18 tokens, B: 19 tokens. That explains some of the delta for the short prompt tails. also saw subtle whitespace normalization differences.

li: another thing: kernel fallback for quant kernels is happening for short sequence lengths in our runtime. profiling shows path A (quant-kernel) used for seq_len>=32, but for seq_len<32 we fall back to the generic matmul path which is several microseconds slower per token. paste of perf log snippet: 
```
[perf] model-B: kernel=quant_conv_v2 seq_len=64 ms/token=2.3 \n[perf] model-B: fallback=matmul_generic seq_len=16 ms/token=3.1 \n```
This matches the synthetic microbench where we forced seq-len=64 vs the convo set where many prompts produce <32 after tokenization.

devon: to isolate, run a synthetic workload that replays the exact token lengths produced by the convo set but using the synth engine so we remove replay-specific overhead. tiny helper i use: 
```python
# synthize prompt lengths
lengths = load('convo-200.tokenlens')\nfor l in lengths:\n  synth_request(seq_len=l, model='model-B', batch=1)
```
That will show whether the kernel selection threshold is the main driver.

jonathan: also confirm both runs used the same compile flags and kernel library version. iirc we had a kernel tweak landed in runtime v1.8 that changes workspace tiling which could affect short-seq perf.

mira: confirmed: replay runs were on runtime v1.8.2+patch, synth runs were on v1.8.2 (no patch). patch note: "quant_conv_v2 tiled fallback fix" — might be the regression. filing issue now.

replay-bot: run-summary: id=run-2026-03-07-1825 models=[A,B] harnesses=[replay,synth] p50_diff=6% p99_diff=14% median_throughput_diff=batch=8 -> 10% lower for model-B when using convo token lengths. artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/runs/run-1825004321/

samir: also double-check stop-sequence implementation: replay harness strips final stop tokens post-decode while synth injects an explicit EOS token. that mismatch can change token counts by +1 in corner cases (trailing spaces).

mira: todo list: 1) reproduce with synth using convo token-lens (devon). 2) pin both runs to same runtime patch and re-run (jonathan). 3) normalize tokenizers to NFC and re-tokenize convo set (samir). 4) instrument kernel selection logs at debug level (li). i'll open a GH issue and tag owners. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/issues/1427 :eyes:

devon: i'll run step (1) tonight and drop raw logs + p99 flamegraphs. expect to see the fallback path show up if li's theory holds.

mira: thanks all — if we confirm kernel fallback is the root cause we should consider lowering the threshold or adding fastpath for seq_len in [8..31]. i suspect perf hit is small at throughput 8+ but visible at p99 for single-request latency.

jonathan: agreed. also let's add a tiny unit in our apples-to-apples checklist: "tokenizer normalization + stop behavior + runtime kernel version" so future runs are consistent.

mira: adding checklist to PR and will update the run doc.

replay-bot: attached: /artifacts/run-1825004321/summary.json (uploaded)

mira: closing loop here once devon posts logs. :thumbsup:
